mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals a contractionary monetary policy cycle, raising discount rates applied to equity cash flows and compressing future returns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year window, or 20-day forward returns in contractionary periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing growth prospects and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not decline significantly (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses above 5.0, or returns remain negative in >60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDP demand (GDPC1) and supply capacity (INDPRO) signals robust economic expansion, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between GDPC1 and INDPRO fails to predict positive returns (Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year window) or returns remain non-significant (t-test p>0.05) despite the proxies' movements.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, rising housing demand (HOUST) signals sustained momentum in the housing sector, driving broader market optimism and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: late-cycle expansion regime and HOUST rises
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not rise significantly (t-test p>0.05) when HOUST increases in a late-cycle expansion, or returns remain negative despite the housing demand surge.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not decline significantly (t-test p>0.05) when FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0%, or returns remain positive despite the rate hike.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and rise in job growth (PAYEMS) reflects strengthening labor market conditions, fostering investor confidence and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS fails to predict significant positive returns (Rank IC <0.03 over 2-year window) or returns remain non-significant (t-test p>0.05) despite the labor indicators' movements.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the supply index (INDPRO) signals contraction in production capacity, reducing growth prospects and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not decline significantly (t-test p>0.05) when INDPRO falls, or returns remain positive despite the supply contraction.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rates increase discount rates applied to equity cash flows, compressing future returns and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not decline significantly (t-test p>0.05) during a tightening cycle when FEDFUNDS rise, or returns remain positive despite the rate increases.
